subject: Structured uplift + overage insurance — renewal amendment discussion
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam@bluemint.ai>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: structured uplift + overage insurance for renewal

Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. Per our call, I wanted to put a concrete proposal on the table that addresses BlueMint's two priorities for the upcoming renewal: (1) predictable unit economics during the first 12 months of the new term while you scale models, and (2) a safety net for unexpected spikes as you onboard two new product lines.

High-level proposal (details attached):
- 12-month renewal term, effective 2027-05-01.
- Committed monthly token floor: 200M tokens/month at $0.0045/token (3% reduction vs current list) — this preserves a predictable base rate.
- Tiered add-on blocks: additional 100M tokens blocks at $0.0039/token up to 400M additional/month.
- Overage insurance (new): For any usage above committed + blocks in a given month, Redwood will apply an overage insurance cap so that effective overage rate won’t exceed $0.0065/token; excess beyond a monthly threshold triggers a credit schedule instead of immediate invoice shock.
- One-time onboarding credit: $25k credit applied over first 3 invoices to offset migration/config costs.

Why this helps BlueMint: predictable floor for budgeting, runway-friendly add-on pricing, and a capped overage path during bursty model training events.

Next steps: if this looks directionally right I can loop in Ben for the finance breakdown and Vanessa for the technical ramp plan; we can also share a short amendment draft for procurement.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the numbers.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0127

Attachment: BLUEMINT_Renewal_Uplift_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet: proposed tiers + monthly example invoice)

From: Sam Patel <sam@bluemint.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@bluemint.ai
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: structured uplift + overage insurance for renewal

Marissa —

Appreciate the detailed outline and the spreadsheet. Overall this aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifying points from our side:

1) The commit floor looks reasonable, but our CFO wants an option to ladder the commit over the first 3 months (e.g., 120M / 160M / 200M) to reduce near-term cash outflow during the Q2 hiring pause. Is Redwood open to a phased ramp with pro-rata pricing on the early months?

2) On the overage insurance: the $0.0065 cap is helpful, but procurement asks that any credit triggered for extreme spikes be applied as a credit against the following invoice (not as a rebate request) and have a clear definition of what qualifies as an "extreme spike" (we suggested > 40% over committed+blocks for the month).

3) Can you add a short clause in the amendment that restricts the insurance mechanism to non-malicious bursts (i.e., exclude bad actor usage and internal testing that wasn't coordinated)?

If you can incorporate those items, procurement is comfortable moving to redlines. We can also do a 30-min call early next week.

—Sam
Head of Platform | BlueMint Analytics
sam@bluemint.ai

Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: structured uplift + overage insurance for renewal

Hi Sam —

Thanks — good asks. Quick responses inline: 

1) Phased ramp: yes, we can do a 3-month laddered commit (120M / 160M / 200M) with the committed pricing applied pro-rata each month; the remainder of the term reverts to the 200M standard monthly floor. I'll include the math examples in the attachment.

2) Overage credit trigger: agree to the credit-on-next-invoice model. We propose the threshold at >35% over committed+blocks for a month to trigger the insurance credit schedule (slightly tighter than your suggested 40% so BlueMint has faster protection). We will document precise calculation examples.

3) Exclusions: we'll include an exclusions clause for obviously non-production or abusive traffic (e.g., API keys flagged for compromise, clearly explained load testing). For internal/partner testing, if BlueMint notifies us in advance we can exclude that usage from the spike calculation.

Ben — looping you in to confirm finance is comfortable with the ramp math and the credit treatment. Vanessa — can you outline a short ramp plan (key milestones and touchpoints) so we can include a technical milestone schedule in the amendment?

If Ben/Vanessa confirm, I'll generate a one-page amendment and send to procurement for redlines by Wednesday.

Best,
Marissa

From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: structured uplift + overage insurance for renewal

All —

Checked the numbers. Finance confirms the laddered commit (120/160/200M) works; we model the total committed tokens over 12 months and apply the blended unit price accordingly for billing illustrations. The onboarding credit ($25k) will be applied as a negative line item across invoices 1–3.

For the overage insurance credit mechanism, we recommend the following concrete schedule to keep accounting clean:
- If monthly usage > (committed + blocks) * 1.35, Redwood issues a credit equal to 50% of the incremental spend up to (committed + blocks) * 1.6.
- Any incremental spend above 1.6x is billed at the standard overage rate and not creditable.

This approach gives BlueMint a predictable cushion while keeping worst-case exposure bounded. Legal can convert this into amendment language.

-ben
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Hi Marissa / Ben —

Procurement reviewed the model and the credit trigger schedule. One request from our side: can Redwood add a 60-day review clause after the first quarter of the new term where both parties can reconvene to rebase committed blocks if actual usage diverges materially (>20% variance) from forecast? We want a safety valve to avoid sustained under/over-commit.

Also, please include a short definition of what constitutes "coordinated testing" to avoid ambiguity about exclusions.

If you can accept those two items, we will route the amendment to legal for redline.

Thanks —
Procurement Team
BlueMint Analytics
procurement@bluemint.ai

I've attached a draft one-page amendment and the updated spreadsheet showing the laddered commit math and the credit schedule examples. If that looks good, please confirm and we'll issue the amendment for legal redlines (DocuSign-ready).
